_comment: How every client frames the home hero, after the mockup Warren VPN Accueil (default tweaks: 380x620 window, scene 'Equilibree' 300px, fade 'Doux'). The hero is hero_height_ratio of its width tall (plus the status bar on a phone); on a phone it grows to absorb free height up to hero_max_height_ratio of its width (the most the width-fit canvas still covers). On a screen wider than tall and shorter than split_below_height_px (a phone in landscape) the hero and the panel sit side by side: the hero is the left half at full height, the panel and the footer scroll on the right. While the connection details are open it shrinks to compact_height_ratio of its width. The three registered scenery layers are drawn in one canvas rect, the header floats over the top and the art fades into the page along mask_stops. A framing names a span of canvas rows that must stay clear between the header (clear_top_px) and the point where that fade reaches half opacity (clear_bottom_fraction of the hero height, given to the formula as fade_px = height * (1 - clear_bottom_fraction)): the cameras, the burrow and Bula down to his tail whenever he is out (ground), the country's skyline down to below its flag once he is in (sky). The canvas is drawn at width-fit unless the span cannot fit, then it narrows and centres. Its top sits flush with the hero top when it can; it drops (headroom) only when a skyline would otherwise sit under the header, and rises only when the span bottom would pass the half-opacity point. A compact hero keeps the scale the same hero has at full height (full_hero_height_px; width-fit on the desktop window and on phones) and pins the span top under the header, the span bottom going into the fade: opening the details slides the art up, it never zooms into it. The rows above a dropped canvas take the landscape's topFill from scenery.json; the columns beside a narrowed canvas show the same landscape at cover scale blurred by margin_blur_px (an ambient wash, no recognisable shape); the canvas edges facing either are feathered over feather_rows canvas rows.

ground.provenance: top_row: 10 rows above the higher camera (plaine.webp, the left camera housing starts at row 330). bottom_row: Bula's tail (bula.webp), just above the bottom of the burrow mouth (rows 759 to 920); with the canvas at width-fit on the 380px window this puts the cameras where the mockup draws them.

sky.top_row: skylineTopRow of the landscape in scenery.json
sky.provenance: bottom_row: below the foot of every flag and landmark of the country plates (flags span rows 427 to about 620), above the top of the burrow mouth (row 759).

formula: hero_height = hero_width * hero_height_ratio (+ the status bar inset on a phone); a phone may grow it up to hero_width * hero_max_height_ratio to take free height; compact: hero_width * compact_height_ratio
y_min = clear_top_px - span_top * scale ; y_max = clear_bottom - span_bottom * scale

compact: scale = the full-height scale of the same hero, min(hero_width / canvas_px[0], (full_hero_height_px * clear_bottom_fraction - clear_top_px) / (span_bottom - span_top)) ; canvas_left as above ; canvas_top = clear_top_px - span_top * scale
the hero's alpha follows mask_stops ([fraction of the hero height, alpha]) from its top to its bottom
